# awscc_mediaconnect_destination_endpoint (Data Source)

Data Source schema for AWS::MediaConnect::DestinationEndpoint



<!-- schema generated by tfplugindocs -->
## Schema

### Required

- `id` (String) Uniquely identifies the resource.

### Read-Only

- `arn` (String)
- `associated_resource_details` (Attributes) The details of the resource that is associated with a destination endpoint. This is a union type, so exactly one of its members is set, depending on the type of the destination endpoint. (see [below for nested schema](#nestedatt--associated_resource_details))
- `availability_zone` (String) The Availability Zone in which the destination endpoint is located.
- `availability_zone_id` (String) The ID of the Availability Zone in which the destination endpoint is located.
- `configuration` (Attributes) The configuration settings for a destination endpoint. This is a union type, so exactly one of its members is set, depending on the type of the destination endpoint. (see [below for nested schema](#nestedatt--configuration))
- `connection_state` (String)
- `created_at` (String) The date and time when the destination endpoint was created.
- `description` (String) The description of the destination endpoint.
- `destination_endpoint_id` (String) The unique identifier of the destination endpoint.
- `destination_type` (String)
- `lifecycle_management` (String)
- `name` (String) The name of the destination endpoint.
- `region_name` (String) The name of the Amazon Web Services Region in which the destination endpoint is located.
- `registration_state` (String)
- `tags` (Attributes List) The tags associated with the destination endpoint. Each tag is a key-value pair. (see [below for nested schema](#nestedatt--tags))
- `updated_at` (String) The date and time when the destination endpoint was last updated.

### Nested Schema for `configuration.standard`

Read-Only:

- `destination_networking_configuration` (Attributes) The networking configuration for a standard destination endpoint. This is a union type, so exactly one of its members is set: public for a publicly accessible endpoint, or vpc for an endpoint in a virtual private cloud (VPC). (see [below for nested schema](#nestedatt--configuration--standard--destination_networking_configuration))
- `destination_networking_type` (String)
- `name` (String) The name of the destination endpoint.
- `protocol` (String)
- `protocol_configuration` (Attributes) The protocol configuration for a standard destination endpoint. This is a union type, so exactly one of its members is set, depending on the protocol that the destination endpoint uses. (see [below for nested schema](#nestedatt--configuration--standard--protocol_configuration))

<a id="nestedatt--configuration--standard--destination_networking_configuration"></a>
### Nested Schema for `configuration.standard.destination_networking_configuration`

Read-Only:

- `public` (Attributes) The networking configuration for a publicly accessible destination endpoint, including the CIDR blocks that are allowed to connect. (see [below for nested schema](#nestedatt--configuration--standard--destination_networking_configuration--public))
- `vpc` (Attributes) The networking configuration for a destination endpoint in a virtual private cloud (VPC). (see [below for nested schema](#nestedatt--configuration--standard--destination_networking_configuration--vpc))

<a id="nestedatt--configuration--standard--destination_networking_configuration--public"></a>
### Nested Schema for `configuration.standard.destination_networking_configuration.public`

Read-Only:

- `destination_allow_rules` (Attributes List) The rules that specify which CIDR blocks can connect to the destination endpoint. You can specify up to 10 rules. (see [below for nested schema](#nestedatt--configuration--standard--destination_networking_configuration--public--destination_allow_rules))

<a id="nestedatt--configuration--standard--destination_networking_configuration--public--destination_allow_rules"></a>
### Nested Schema for `configuration.standard.destination_networking_configuration.public.destination_allow_rules`

Read-Only:

- `cidr` (String) The CIDR block that is allowed to connect to the destination endpoint, in CIDR notation.



<a id="nestedatt--configuration--standard--destination_networking_configuration--vpc"></a>
### Nested Schema for `configuration.standard.destination_networking_configuration.vpc`

Read-Only:

- `security_group_ids` (List of String) The IDs of the security groups to associate with the destination endpoint. You can specify from 1 to 5 security groups.
- `subnet_id` (String) The ID of the subnet to use for the destination endpoint.



<a id="nestedatt--configuration--standard--protocol_configuration"></a>
### Nested Schema for `configuration.standard.protocol_configuration`

Read-Only:

- `rist` (Attributes) The configuration settings for a destination endpoint that uses the RIST protocol. (see [below for nested schema](#nestedatt--configuration--standard--protocol_configuration--rist))
- `rtp` (Attributes) The configuration settings for a destination endpoint that uses the RTP protocol. (see [below for nested schema](#nestedatt--configuration--standard--protocol_configuration--rtp))
- `srt_caller` (Attributes) The configuration settings for a destination endpoint that uses SRT in caller mode. (see [below for nested schema](#nestedatt--configuration--standard--protocol_configuration--srt_caller))
- `srt_listener` (Attributes) The configuration settings for a destination endpoint that uses SRT in listener mode. (see [below for nested schema](#nestedatt--configuration--standard--protocol_configuration--srt_listener))

<a id="nestedatt--configuration--standard--protocol_configuration--rist"></a>
### Nested Schema for `configuration.standard.protocol_configuration.rist`

Read-Only:

- `destination_address` (String) The IP address on which the destination endpoint receives content.
- `destination_ingest_port` (Number) The port on which the destination endpoint receives content. The valid range is 1024 to 65531.


<a id="nestedatt--configuration--standard--protocol_configuration--rtp"></a>
### Nested Schema for `configuration.standard.protocol_configuration.rtp`

Read-Only:

- `destination_address` (String) The IP address on which the destination endpoint receives content.
- `destination_ingest_port` (Number) The port on which the destination endpoint receives content. The valid range is 1024 to 65531.
- `forward_error_correction_state` (String)


<a id="nestedatt--configuration--standard--protocol_configuration--srt_caller"></a>
### Nested Schema for `configuration.standard.protocol_configuration.srt_caller`

Read-Only:

- `encryption_passphrase` (Attributes) The configuration for the Secrets Manager secret that holds the key or passphrase used to encrypt an endpoint connection. (see [below for nested schema](#nestedatt--configuration--standard--protocol_configuration--srt_caller--encryption_passphrase))
- `minimum_latency_milliseconds` (Number) The minimum latency, in milliseconds, for the SRT connection. The valid range is 10 to 10000.
- `source_listener_port` (Number) The port on which the source listens for the connection. The valid range is 3000 to 30000.

<a id="nestedatt--configuration--standard--protocol_configuration--srt_caller--encryption_passphrase"></a>
### Nested Schema for `configuration.standard.protocol_configuration.srt_caller.encryption_passphrase`

Read-Only:

- `secret_arn` (String) The ARN of the Secrets Manager secret that holds the key or passphrase. The secret must be encrypted with a customer managed Amazon Web Services KMS key that is enabled and symmetric; it cannot use the Amazon Web Services managed key aws/secretsmanager. The secret must be in the same Amazon Web Services account and Region as the endpoint.



<a id="nestedatt--configuration--standard--protocol_configuration--srt_listener"></a>
### Nested Schema for `configuration.standard.protocol_configuration.srt_listener`

Read-Only:

- `destination_address` (String) The IP address on which the destination endpoint listens for incoming connections.
- `destination_ingest_port` (Number) The port on which the destination endpoint listens for incoming connections. The valid range is 0 to 65531.
- `encryption_passphrase` (Attributes) The configuration for the Secrets Manager secret that holds the key or passphrase used to encrypt an endpoint connection. (see [below for nested schema](#nestedatt--configuration--standard--protocol_configuration--srt_listener--encryption_passphrase))
- `minimum_latency_milliseconds` (Number) The minimum latency, in milliseconds, for the SRT connection. The valid range is 10 to 10000.
- `stream_id` (String) The stream ID that identifies the content for the SRT connection.

<a id="nestedatt--configuration--standard--protocol_configuration--srt_listener--encryption_passphrase"></a>
### Nested Schema for `configuration.standard.protocol_configuration.srt_listener.encryption_passphrase`

Read-Only:

- `secret_arn` (String) The ARN of the Secrets Manager secret that holds the key or passphrase. The secret must be encrypted with a customer managed Amazon Web Services KMS key that is enabled and symmetric; it cannot use the Amazon Web Services managed key aws/secretsmanager. The secret must be in the same Amazon Web Services account and Region as the endpoint.
